<reason>Side A wins by replacing a passport cap with a bed-conditioned enrollment rule that answers PRO's immediacy and discretionary-growth pressures on the same admissions cycle, while exposing that a cap frees mostly re-lettable student rooms, delivers no specified family housing benefit, and cuts revenue needed for domestic places and accommodation. B's threshold answer still risks an open-ended brake and its refusal to quantify housing relief weakened its burden.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>Side A's Rebuttal 2 was decisive: A1/A2 directly offered master-leases and secured-bed offers as immediate protection, then showed B's answers supplied no family-home metric and relied on a vacancy trigger that could persist for years.</best_rebuttal>
